02 Story: On the last night before his lighthouse is automated, an old Kerala keeper who has burned his lamp for forty years for a son lost at sea keeps it alive through a storm to guide home a small boat he cannot name.
Added: Genre, tone, theme and world description
Added: Character names (Raghavan, Anil), looks, ages, wants, needs and arcs

On the last night before his lighthouse is automated, an old Kerala keeper who has burned his lamp for forty years for a son lost at sea keeps it alive through a storm to guide home a small boat he cannot name.
Quiet, aching, ultimately consoling; hushed and elegiac, with a swell of hope at the end.
Love outlasts loss when it becomes service to others; a vigil kept for one can save many.

The Kerala coast at dusk and night: a weathered whitewashed lighthouse on a laterite headland, coconut palms bent by wind, a small fishing harbour with wooden boats, monsoon-edged sea. Intimate keeper's quarters with an oil lamp, a faded photograph and a folded work order. Vertical 9:16 for Instagram Reels, Malayalam with minimal or no dialogue and English subtitles if any speech.

Protagonist, the lighthouse keeper. Late 60s. Lean, weathered, white stubble, faded khaki shirt and mundu, brass-rimmed glasses, hands scarred from years of lamp work.. Wants: To keep the lamp burning one last night, as he has every night, in case his son returns.. Needs: To accept the loss and let his vigil become a gift to others, so he can let go.. Arc: From a man clinging to a hopeless wait, to one who understands the light was always meant to bring someone home, and finally rests.

The lost son, seen only in a photograph and memory. Early 20s in the photo. Smiling young fisherman, wet hair, striped shirt, standing by a wooden boat.. Wants: (Absent) To come home.. Needs: (Symbolic) To be remembered with peace, not only grief.. Arc: Remains a memory; his presence is echoed in the boat that arrives.

Unnamed fisherman in the small boat, glimpsed at the end. Around 20s. Silhouetted figure in a rain-soaked shirt, lantern in hand, raising an arm in thanks.. Wants: To survive the storm and reach harbour.. Needs: A guiding light.. Arc: From lost in the dark to safe ashore, standing in for the son who never returned.

Dusk. Raghavan climbs the lighthouse stairs and lights the lamp, as he has for forty years. A faded photo of his son sits by the lamp, and beside it a notice: the lighthouse will be automated after tonight. He looks to the empty sea.

Wind and rain rise. The power flickers and the lamp falters. Midpoint (~0:30): through the rain, tiny boat lights appear on the horizon, tossed by the waves. He doesn't know whose boat it is. He shields the flame, cranks and tends the lamp by hand, hands shaking, while the beam sweeps the water.

The boat reaches the harbour. A young man steps ashore and raises a hand toward the light. Raghavan, exhausted, smiles, touches the photograph, and the dawn breaks as the lamp goes dark for the last time. Final image: the sunrise, the old keeper at peace. Title card: The Last Light.

21 Sound, music and dub: The Last Light: Sound, Music and Dub Plan
A 60-second vertical Reel needs a handful of cues: 4 music cues (score only, one source sound) and 5 key sound design moments, in 3 scenes.
Score is a simple solo piano with soft strings that swell only at the dawn in Scene 3. Whether to use piano or strings is the filmmaker's choice.
Sound design (wind, surf, lamp mechanism, rain, power hum) carries the storm. The lamp's mechanical turn is the film's heartbeat.
Language: Malayalam original with minimal or no speech. English burned-in subtitles only if a line is spoken. No dub needed. Optional silent-safe version for Instagram autoplay.

Music must be royalty-free or AI-generated with a licence that allows Instagram use. Cost: INR 0 beyond existing subscriptions (planning estimate). Timings are planning estimates from the shot plan (about 20s, 22s, 18s).

Hushed, elegiac. Sparse solo piano, a few slow notes under the stairs climb and the lighting of the lamp. Leaves space for the photograph of Anil and the folded notice. Fades to near silence on the empty sea.

Quiet bed: distant surf, light sea wind, boots on iron spiral stairs, the click and low whirr of the lamp mechanism starting. This mechanical turn becomes a recurring beat. Paper rustle as Raghavan folds the notice.

Aching, rising unease. Low sustained strings under the storm, piano thinning out. Dips almost to nothing when the power flickers, then rebuilds as the boat's lights appear. No drums, so the emotion stays human.

Wind through the palms, rain hitting the lamp glass, rolling waves on rocks. A power hum drops out at the flicker, the lamp mechanism slows and strains, then Raghavan's hand-turning (creak, breathing, shaky effort) takes over as the rhythm. Distant thunder.
Faint wooden creak and wave slap from the small boat, tiny lantern clink. Beam sweep whoosh timed to each turn. Release of tension when the boat clears the rocks: waves soften.

Consoling, a swell of hope. Strings open up and the piano carries a warm theme as the boat enters the harbour, the boatman raises an arm and Raghavan touches Anil's photograph. The one emotional peak of the film.
Storm dies away. Gentle waves, early birdsong (gulls, crows), the lamp mechanism winding down to a final stop, so the lamp's rest is heard. Harbour water lapping against the hull.
Resolving, a soft final piano note that rings out under the title 'The Last Light'. Ends on a held sea-air tone, no hard stop.
